part1.label: About Silver Peak Design Build
part1.title: Built for Major Residential Projects.
part1.text: Silver Peak Design Build is a residential design-build contractor serving North Seattle and select Eastside communities, focused on whole-house renovations, builds, rebuilds, and major additions.

Years of construction experience. Silver Peak is led by Craig Mauer and works with a trusted team of designers, craftspeople, and project partners on residential projects in North Seattle and select Eastside communities.

part2.label: Our Story
part2.heading: Built for Bigger Projects.
part2.text1: One team handles planning, design, permits, and construction for substantial residential projects.
part2.text2: Founder Craig Mauer brings more than 20 years of hands-on residential construction experience.
part2.text3: We take on projects based on scope, location, schedule, and fit.

part3.label: Why Silver Peak
part3.heading: What Homeowners Value.
part3.text: We plan around site conditions, communicate clearly, and bring residential construction experience to each project.

part1.text: A consistent point of contact helps homeowners track decisions and next steps.

part2.text: We review the property, project goals, budget direction, and construction needs early.

part3.text: We concentrate on North Seattle and select Eastside projects north of I-90 so site visits, communication, and project oversight remain practical.

part4.text: Our work is built around durable materials, clean details, and lasting value for the people living in the home.

part4.label: Where We Focus
part4.heading: Projects We Build.
part4.text: Whole-house renovations, builds and rebuilds come first, followed by major additions. Next are ADUs, DADUs, and basement remodels; kitchens, bathrooms, and specialty work are considered selectively.

part1.text: Full-home renovations and rebuilds involving structural work or coordinated changes across the property.

part2.text: Major additions that add living space and connect the new construction to the existing home.

part3.text: Detached and attached living spaces planned around site conditions, access, privacy, utilities, zoning, and permit requirements.

part4.text: Substantial lower-level renovations that can create finished living areas, bedrooms, storage, built-ins, or additional dwelling space.

part5.text: Select kitchen and bathroom remodels when the project scope, schedule, location, and overall fit align with the team.

part6.text: Selected exterior improvements, porch work, damage restoration, and detail-focused construction that complements larger residential projects.

part5.label: How We Work
part5.heading: Project Fit Comes First.
part5.text: A technical site assessment is not the first step for every inquiry. We first review the location, project type, scope, budget direction, and working fit. Qualified projects then move to an in-person technical site assessment.
part5.item1: **Project Review & Fit Call**We review your location, goals, project type, scope, budget range, timeline, and whether the project is a good working fit.
part5.item2: **Technical Site Assessment**Qualified projects move to an in-person review of existing conditions, access, structure, utilities, constraints, and feasibility.
part5.item3: **Design & Permits**We connect layout decisions, materials, scope, permit needs, scheduling, and build strategy before construction begins.
part5.item4: **Construction**We manage the build with coordinated communication, quality craftsmanship, and attention to the agreed scope.

part6.label: Start Your Project
part6.heading: Start With a Project Review.
part6.text: Tell us the location, project type, scope, and budget direction. If the project is a fit for our service area and the work we are set up to do, we will talk through the next step and determine whether a technical site assessment makes sense.

part7.label: Meet the Owner
part7.title: Meet Craig Mauer.
part7.text1: Craig works directly with homeowners to understand project scope and existing site conditions.
part7.text2: His field experience helps identify construction questions while plans are still taking shape.
part7.text3: He keeps decisions practical and expectations clear.
part7.text4: On whole-house projects, a change in one area can affect work elsewhere.

part8.label: Plan With Confidence
part8.heading: Talk With the Builder.
part8.text: Have a whole-house build, addition, DADU, ADU, basement, kitchen, or bathroom project in mind? Start by sharing the location, scope, budget direction, and goals so we can first determine whether the project is a fit.

part9.label: Our Process
part9.title: Project Fit Comes First.
part9.text: Silver Peak does not schedule a technical site assessment for every inquiry. We first review location, project type, scope, budget direction, and working fit. Qualified projects then move into site assessment, planning, and construction.

part1.text: We start with your location, goals, project type, scope, budget range, timeline, and overall working fit. One or more calls may happen before an in-person visit is scheduled.

part2.text: Qualified projects move to an in-person review of existing conditions, access, structural limits, utilities, site constraints, and overall feasibility.

part3.text: We connect layout direction, materials, finishes, scope, permit requirements, scheduling, and build strategy so the project is better prepared before construction.

part4.text: Once scope and planning are defined, construction moves ahead with coordinated communication, quality craftsmanship, and attention to the agreed project plan.

part11.text1: Every project starts by confirming that Silver Peak is a good fit for the homeowner and that the project is a good fit for Silver Peak.
part11.item1: Project type, location, and scope review
part11.item3: One or more fit calls when needed
part11.item4: Technical site assessment for qualified projects
part11.item5: Design, permits, construction communication, and sequencing
part11.heading: Clarity Before Commitment.
part11.text2: Reviewing location, scope, budget, and fit before an in-person site assessment helps both the homeowner and the Silver Peak team use their time well and move forward with clearer expectations.
part11.text3: This process is designed first for whole-house builds and rebuilds, additions, DADUs, ADUs, and basement remodels, with select kitchen and bathroom projects considered when the overall fit is right.

part12.label: Next Step
part12.heading: Let’s Talk About Your Project.
part12.text: If you are planning a project in North Seattle or the Eastside north of I-90, start by sharing the project location, scope, and budget direction so we can determine the right next step.

part13.label: Core Service Area
part13.title: North Seattle & Eastside, North of I-90.
part13.text: Silver Peak focuses on North Seattle and Eastside communities north of I-90. Within that broader area, we prefer northern routes and communities where site visits, construction oversight, and communication can stay practical.

part14.heading: North Seattle and the Northern Eastside.
part14.text1: Our normal market is north of I-90, with our main focus on North Seattle and northern Eastside communities. When possible, we prefer projects north of SR 520 so travel, site visits, and construction oversight stay practical.
part14.text2: Our primary northern focus includes Bothell, Mill Creek, and Woodinville, along with North Seattle. We also consider select projects in Redmond and Kirkland when the location, scope, budget, timing, and working fit make sense.
part14.short: **Outside our normal service area:** Projects south of I-90 are generally outside Silver Peak’s coverage area.
part14.subheading:
North Seattle\
Bothell · Mill Creek · Woodinville\
Select Redmond · Kirkland
part14.text3: A focused service area helps Silver Peak stay responsive with project reviews, technical site assessments, construction visits, and ongoing project management.

part15.label: Where We Work
part15.heading: Clear Geography. Better Project Fit.
part15.text: Silver Peak keeps its service area intentionally focused: North Seattle and Eastside projects north of I-90, with a preference for northern communities and routes north of SR 520 when possible.

part16.label: Check Your Project Fit
part16.heading: Start With a Project Review.
part16.text: If your project is in North Seattle or on the Eastside north of I-90, send us the address, project type, scope, and budget direction. We will confirm location and project fit before scheduling a technical site assessment.
